$comment: THE HOST SPECIFICATIONS THIS TREE MAKES CLAIMS ABOUT, PINNED BY REVISION.
Every binding and placement asserts things about a protocol it does not own — that x402 reserves two
keys in `extra`, that UCP binds authority to the `schema` URL alone, that Verifiable Intent rejects
unknown constraint types in open mandates. Those assertions were true when they were read, and nothing
in this repository could tell when they stopped being true: they were pinned by DATE. A date cannot be
checked. Measured 2026-08-12, shipped source carried thirty-six date-pinned host claims and about ten
`drift-guard.yml` already solves this for the one host that is a contract: it reads the deployed escrow
weekly and compares against derivations transcribed from a pinned commit. This file is the same idea one
level up, for hosts that are SPECIFICATIONS rather than chains. `pnpm spec-drift` is its runner, and it
is run BY HAND: this repository stands alone, and a scheduled job against eight third-party APIs would
be a standing dependency on other people's uptime for something that cannot make a payment go wrong.
`readAt` is the last commit touching `paths` at the moment this tree read them — path-scoped, because a
typo fix in a host's README is not drift in its specification. `status` is the claim this file makes:
`current` means the tree agrees with that revision, `drifted` means the host has moved and the re-read
is owed. A `drifted` entry is a recorded debt, not a broken gate, which is why the weekly job fails only
on a `current` entry that moved. An entry that is permanently red is an entry everyone learns to ignore.

hosts.note: The §6.1 reserved keys and paymentFlow axis landed in this very commit. Nine published extensions, all inlining a complete JSON Schema; Bazaar forbids an external $ref.
Ten charge methods. The core scheme has two identities: paymentauth.org publishes draft-httpauth-payment-00, the IETF datatracker mirrors it as draft-ryan-httpauth-payment-01.

Moved 2026-08-12 in 3b9a8dfe7c, which reserves the `ucp` member as a protocol namespace and adds map_order. Read on the day: it constrains where EXTENSION data may sit and forbids defining a domain field named `ucp`. This tree's carrier is a policies[] entry and its reader consumes UCP's own ucp.capabilities, so no claim here is affected — but the full re-read against overview.md and ucp.json is owed before the pin advances.

open_checkout_mandate.json: five members, constraints a closed two-member anyOf, contains line_items. Its constraint type ids carry no `mandate.` prefix, so AP2 and Verifiable Intent do NOT share a vocabulary.
AgentExtension has four fields — uri, description, required, params — which v1.38 §C.8 now states too.
Eight registered constraint types, all underscored. Open mandates MUST reject unknown constraint types regardless of strictness mode — the reason this placement is declaration-only.
CheckoutSessionBase is additionalProperties:false and CheckoutSession a bare allOf over it, which is why v1.38 §C.2 withdrew the top-level carrier.

DELIBERATELY NOT TRACKING HEAD, which is why the drift job skips it. This is the DEPLOYED revision — v1.0.0 plus eleven commits — and it is the gitlink of lib/commerce-payments. Upstream moving is expected and irrelevant; what would matter is the deployed contract diverging from these transcriptions, and drift-guard.yml reads the live chain weekly to check exactly that. This entry pins the source a human reads; that job pins the bytecode a payment meets.

Published behind Visa Developer rather than in a public repository. Same treatment as TIP-20: re-read by hand, and the load-bearing claim — that Signature-Input covers exactly "@authority" "@path" — is quoted verbatim in the package so a reader can check it against whatever Visa publishes today.
